commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: Extract repeated task display loop
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI repeats the same numbered-task loop in three display methods.
Keeping those copies separate makes small output changes harder to apply
consistently.

Extract the shared loop into one private helper so each public display
method focuses on its heading and empty-state behaviour.

Document the repository's subject, body, branch, and message-format requirements.

Provide a project-local reference so future commits follow the stricter
requirement that every commit includes a rationale-bearing body.

State that the convention requires complete commit messages.

Make the purpose of the documented requirement explicit for contributors.

Task constructors rely on callers to provide non-null dates and valid
event ranges. These assumptions are important because later operations
use the values without defensive checks.

Add Java assertions at the construction boundaries to document and
verify those invariants when assertions are enabled.

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Use streams for read-only queries
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList uses manual loops for filtering operations that only select
existing tasks. The loops obscure the query intent and duplicate result
collection logic.

Use ordered streams for date and keyword queries while returning the
existing mutable-copy API expected by the rest of the application.

Merge the assertions increment into master through its fork-local pull
request so task invariants are documented in the main tree.

Synchronise the code-quality increment with the merged assertions
increment before updating its pull request.

Synchronise the streams increment with the merged assertions
increment before updating its pull request.

Merge the code-quality increment after synchronising it with the
assertions increment through its fork-local pull request.

Synchronise the streams increment with the merged code-quality
increment before completing its pull request.

Merge the streams increment after synchronising it with the
assertions and code-quality increments through its fork-local pull
request.

Users can inspect tasks in a meaningful order without changing the order
used by task numbers, storage, or existing commands.

Add a sort command that displays a case-insensitive alphabetical copy,
with parser, UI, task-list, and command-test support.

Merge the completed category C sort extension into master while keeping
BCD-Extension on the feature commit that introduces it.

The GUI offered only a transcript and a single command field, which made common actions less discoverable and provided little feedback about the current task list.\n\nAdd a task-count status indicator, quick-action buttons, transcript reset support, keyboard-friendly command handling, and a clearer visual hierarchy so the GUI is more useful during normal task management.

Merge the completed Better GUI increment into master.\n\nKeep the feature branch history visible so the Week 6 optional enhancement follows the project workflow and the improved JavaFX workspace is available on the submission branch.

Matthew's responses were functional but indistinguishable from a generic task manager, which made the product feel unfinished.\n\nGive the CLI and GUI the same lightly humorous personality while retaining the established task details and response phrases used by existing tests and documentation.

Merge the completed personality increment into master.\n\nKeep Matthew's responses consistent between the CLI and GUI so the product has a recognisable voice without changing command semantics or persisted data.

Null commands, end-of-file input, and malformed saved events could escape the normal user-facing error path. The GUI could also become unusable if an unexpected runtime failure occurred while processing a command.\n\nValidate these boundary cases, stop the CLI cleanly at end of input, reject corrupt persisted records with helpful messages, and keep the GUI responsive after unexpected command-processing failures.

Merge the completed error-handling increment into master.\n\nEnsure malformed commands, incomplete input streams, corrupt task files, and unexpected GUI failures are handled without crashing or trapping the product in an unusable state.

The new boundary handling needs tests that protect it from regressions, especially because these paths are difficult to exercise through the JavaFX window.\n\nCover null commands, EOF-driven shutdown, corrupt task records, reversed event ranges, and buffered GUI responses with focused JUnit tests that run without a display.

Merge the completed testing increment into master.\n\nPreserve regression coverage for malformed input, end-of-file behaviour, corrupt storage, and display buffering so the Week 6 enhancements remain verifiable.

The Week 6 enhancements were produced with AI assistance, but the repository did not record where that assistance was used or how the resulting code was reviewed.\n\nDocument the AI collaboration and review scope so reused ideas are credited transparently and the final product is ready for course review.
Merge the finalisation work into master.\n\nRecord how AI-assisted changes were used and reviewed so the product satisfies the course's transparency and reuse-credit expectations before submission.

commitResults.messageTitle: Set up the Matthew product website
commitResults.messageBody: The product website still contained template placeholders and had no representative GUI screenshot, so users could not learn the actual command syntax or see the finished product.\n\nAdd a complete user guide covering every command, persistence, error behaviour, and quick actions, together with a single full-window screenshot named docs/Ui.png as required by the iP website task.
Merge the completed product website increment into master.\n\nMake the final product understandable and showcaseable by including the completed user guide and the required full-window GUI screenshot.

Three public methods generated Javadoc warnings because their return or parameter contracts were not documented. Add the missing Javadoc tags so the public API documents its observable behaviour completely and the Javadoc task finishes without warnings.
